# Add getPagePointer for zero-copy memory reads from JS (closes #113)

## Pull Request by @yawningmonsoon

## Summary

- Adds `Memory.getPagePointer(pageIndex: u32): usize` — returns the WASM linear memory byte offset of a page's backing buffer, or `0` on page/access fault (no extra allocations on the WASM side).
- Exports `getPagePointer(page)` from `api-debugger.ts`, deprecating `getMemory`.
- Exports `pvmGetPagePointer(pvmId, page)` from `api-utils.ts`, deprecating `pvmReadMemory`.
- Adds `Assert.isNotEqual` to the test helpers.
- Adds 5 tests in `memory.test.ts` covering fault cases and data-correctness via raw pointer reads.

### JS-side usage

```ts
let pagesRead = 0;
for (let address = start; address < end; address += PAGE_SIZE) {
  const page = address >> PAGE_SIZE_SHIFT;
  const ptr = getPagePointer(page); // or pvmGetPagePointer(pvmId, page)
  if (ptr === 0) throw new Error(`Page fault at 0x${(page << PAGE_SIZE_SHIFT).toString(16)}`);
  destination.set(
    new Uint8Array(wasm.instance.exports.memory.buffer, ptr, Math.min(end - address, PAGE_SIZE)),
    pagesRead << PAGE_SIZE_SHIFT,
  );
  pagesRead++;
}
```

No extra WASM-side allocations — bytes are copied directly from WASM linear memory.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm run build` passes cleanly
- [ ] `npm test` — all existing tests still pass; 5 new `getPagePointer` tests pass
- [ ] Verify JS callers can replace `getMemory` / `pvmReadMemory` with the pointer-based loop above

Closes #113
